newsitem.title: UK: ASDA sees 300 mln stg off drug prices.
newsitem.headline: ASDA sees 300 mln stg off drug prices.

text.p: British supermarket retailer ASDA Plc welcomed the British government's decision on Friday to seek a ban on price-fixing for non-prescription medicines, claiming it could save 300 million stg for consumers.
The move "could lead to price cuts on everyday healthcare products worth 300 million stg to the British public," ASDA said in a statement.
ASDA chief executive Allan Leighton said the move "signals the beginning of the end for price fixing."
ASDA has campaigned for a year to have Resale Price Maintenance (RPM) removed from over-the-counter medicines, following a successful push to remove RPM from books.
But ASDA will not immediately cut prices of branded products, public relations chief Phil Reed said.
"RPM is still in place, we are still in the same situation we were in yesterday and we will still be in it tomorrow," he told Reuters.
ASDA has also launched a 10-point plan for the renewal of local pharmacies, which have claimed they would be hard hit and face closures if RPM were removed.

ASDA said the plan included enhancing margins for National Health Service prescription fees for small chemists and allowing selected pharmacies to prescribe some medicines, similar to continental systems.
It also backed the existing Essential Small Pharmacy scheme, which aims to support pharmacies in rural locations where they are most needed.

ASDA currently is refusing to sell Anadin Paracetamol, a painkiller produced by Whitehall Laboratories, and large packs of indigestion treatment Alka Seltzer, after ASDA refused to implement higher prices imposed by manufacturers.
